_note: Rothschild breadth pass (11 Nov 2026): family members and institutions with a documented tie to Palestine, Zionism or Israel before 1967 that the map was missing. Each tie carries its own refs.

nodes.name: Rózsika Rothschild
nodes.note: Rózsika Rothschild (née von Wertheimstein, 1870–1940), wife of Charles Rothschild. She brought Chaim Weizmann to her husband and to his brother Walter, and is credited with a key part in the run-up to the Balfour Declaration.

nodes.name: Evelyn Achille de Rothschild
nodes.note: Evelyn Achille de Rothschild (1886–1917), son of Leopold. Major, Buckinghamshire Yeomanry; wounded at Mughar Ridge on 13 November 1917 in the British conquest of Palestine, eleven days after the Balfour Declaration; died 17 November; buried in the Jewish cemetery at Rishon LeZion.

nodes.name: Albert Cohn
nodes.note: Albert Cohn (1814–1877), Paris scholar and the Paris Rothschilds' almoner. Sent to Jerusalem by James de Rothschild in 1854; founded the city's first Jewish hospital, named for Mayer Amschel Rothschild, and a girls' school beside it.

nodes.name: Meyer Rothschild Hospital, Jerusalem (1854)
nodes.note: Jerusalem's first Jewish hospital, founded in 1854 by Albert Cohn for the Paris Rothschilds and named after Mayer Amschel Rothschild. The family's first documented institution in Palestine, 28 years before Edmond's colonies.

nodes.name: Evelina de Rothschild School, Jerusalem
nodes.note: The first girls' school in Jerusalem, opened in 1854 beside the Rothschild hospital. Lionel de Rothschild of London took over its sponsorship in 1867 and named it after his late daughter Evelina.

nodes.name: Herzl's "Address to the Rothschilds" (1895)
nodes.note: Herzl first conceived Der Judenstaat as a speech to the Rothschild family, titled "Address to the Rothschilds". It was never delivered; the pamphlet appeared in February 1896.

nodes.name: Royal Commission on Alien Immigration (1902–03)
nodes.note: British royal commission appointed 21 March 1902, reported 10 August 1903; Lord (Natty) Rothschild was one of its seven members. Herzl gave evidence on 7 July 1902.

nodes.name: Central British Fund for German Jewry (1933)
nodes.note: British refugee-relief fund founded in 1933, with Anthony and Yvonne de Rothschild among its founders and its work coordinated from N M Rothschild's offices at New Court. The Rothschild Archive estimates it rescued 65,000 people in the 1930s and 1940s, including 10,000 children through the Kindertransport.

nodes.name: Edmond Adolphe de Rothschild
nodes.note: Edmond Adolphe de Rothschild (1926–1997), grandson of Edmond and son of Maurice. Signed a 1958 memorandum with the State of Israel on Caesarea; the 1962 agreement made the state a partner in its development.

nodes.name: Edmond de Rothschild Foundation (Israel)
nodes.note: Rothschild family foundation in Israel; established the Caesarea Development Corporation in 1952 and gave about 35,000 dunams around Caesarea to the government, which leased them back to the foundation.

nodes.name: Caesarea Development Corporation (1952)
nodes.note: Founded in 1952 by the Edmond de Rothschild Foundation to develop Caesarea; the state became a partner through a 1958 memorandum and a 1962 agreement.

nodes.name: Bethsabée (Batsheva) de Rothschild
nodes.note: Bethsabée de Rothschild (1914–1999), daughter of Édouard. Moved to Israel; co-founded the Batsheva Dance Company with Martha Graham in 1964.

nodes.name: Batsheva Dance Company (1964)
nodes.note: Israeli dance company founded on 24 December 1964 by Batsheva de Rothschild and Martha Graham.
